author: Newsie (scheduled pre-market run, file 4)
notes: Scores so far 2 of 9 hit (22%, all 50-65 bucket), so confidence stays at 50-55. Board asks applied: fade calls start at 09:45/10:00, not 09:30, and the bias states a lean instead of neutral. Today is the mirror of Nov 20: a huge relief GAP UP after a -8.6% week (S&P correction, Nasdaq ~-5.3% Friday, Friday closed at its lows on SPY 627M shares). Futures, sources disagree by time: S&P +2.1 to +2.9%, Nasdaq 100 +2.9 to +3.6%, Dow +1.7 to +2.1% (05:23-08:15 ET). Reasons given: bargain hunting/short covering in AI and chips, Oracle saying AI contract funding is secured, Korea/China market-support steps. VIX ~30-31 (from 35+), 10y 4.91% (-14bp Friday), WTI ~$82 (-1.5 to -2.3%), gold +2.5-2.9%, BTC flat ~$61k. Fed: ~96% December hike priced (single source). Thanksgiving week: Thu closed, Fri 13:00 ET close, PCE/GDP/durables Wed 08:30 ET; thin volume after Tuesday. The Nov 12/17/18/19 gap-ups all faded from the first minutes, but those were not capitulation follow-ups; after a washout Friday a relief day can run all day. Low conviction both ways. No Skylit credits used (time).

calls.catalyst: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal near $43.9B (1.135 CRWD per ZS, ~34% premium). CRWD about -8 to -9% premarket while the tape is up 2-3%.
calls.macro_link: Idiosyncratic: merger-arb desks short the acquirer against long ZS in all-stock deals, a steady supply that tends to cap acquirer bounces on deal day even in a strong tape.
calls.chart_note: No CRWD bars in our archive. Window starts 10:00 to skip a possible opening squeeze with the market rally; if CRWD reclaims its 09:30-10:00 high, the call is likely wrong.
calls.volume_note: Deal-day volume will be several times normal; not measured pre-market.

calls.catalyst: Gap-fade bet: Nasdaq 100 futures +2.9 to +3.6% after QQQ -5.4% Friday (close 610.04, low 606.23). A +3% gap opens near 628.
calls.macro_link: Rebound is short covering plus bargain hunting; nothing changed on the hike pricing (~96% December) and the AI/chip worries (NVDA leadership change) are unresolved. Lower 10y (4.91%) and softer oil are mild tailwinds against this call.
calls.chart_note: Our bars: every gap-up this month (Nov 12, 17, 18, 19) faded from the first 30 minutes; Nov 19 opened 671 and closed 645. Counter-case: Friday was a capitulation-style close at the low on record volume, and VIX is easing, so a trend-up relief day is quite possible. If QQQ holds above its opening 15-min high after 10:15, this call is likely wrong. Correlated with the SPY bias: one bet, not two.
calls.volume_note: Friday QQQ volume 950M, the heaviest in our archive window; expect high but falling volume today.

market_read.tone: Relief rally: futures up 2-3.5% after a correction week, chips and neoclouds +5-10% premarket, VIX back near 30, yields and oil lower; Thanksgiving week, thin after Tuesday.
market_read.day_type: event-driven (large gap up; early fade then chop is my slight lean, an all-day trend-up relief rally is the main alternative)
market_read.comment: Bias is open-to-close from the gap open, not vs. Friday's close (everything is up vs. Friday). SPY prior close 690.91; a +2.3% gap opens near 707, under Friday's 10:00 high 718.29. The lean comes from this month's gap-up fades and is weak (51/52): a fresh washout often gives a trend-up Monday. If SPY is above its opening 30-min high at 10:30, drop the down bias.

desk_flags.reason: A 2-3% gap makes the 09:30-09:45 range very wide and the 09:45 PMI lands as the range closes; in gap-ups this month the first break up failed. An inverse-ETF break fits my lean; a bull-ETF break is the riskier side, but the lean is weak.
Trend entries suit either outcome (fade or relief trend); no major scheduled release inside the hold after 09:45.
Opening volume spikes will be extreme in both directions on a gap after a record-volume Friday; spikes before 10:00 are mostly noise. Later spikes in the direction of the 10:00-10:30 trend are fine.
